campaignStructure.premise: Player is a Ditto that has taken human form and arrives in a post-apocalyptic, emptied-out Kanto-inspired world. Goal is to rebuild/restore the land and repopulate it with Pokémon by building habitats, homes, and communities. No traditional combat/battling — reviews note the game removes Pokémon fighting entirely.
regions: Withered Wasteland (also referred to as 'Barren Badlands' in one source — name inconsistent across wikis; starting area)
Sparkling Skylands (final of the four main story regions)
Palette Town (secret 5th area, unlocked only after the main story/credits — freeform building area, per thegameswiki)

trainerRankSystem.description: Four-tier rank system (No Rank -> Great -> Ultra -> Master) that gates access to new regions. Rank increases automatically upon completing specific story 'Important Requests' tied to meeting Legendary Pokémon — not a grind/XP system.

ranks.trigger: Complete the 'Yawn Up A Storm' Important Request in Withered Wasteland (raise humidity), leading to meeting Kyogre.
ranks.unlocks: Bleak Beach and Rocky Ridges become accessible.

ranks.trigger: Complete 'Brighten Things Up' in Bleak Beach (meet Raikou) AND 'Time to Party' in Rocky Ridges (meet Volcanion).
Complete 'Rebuild the Huge Building' in Sparkling Skylands, leading to meeting Mewtwo.
ranks.unlocks: Highest rank; no further explorable areas gated by rank specifically, but marks approach to story completion.

trainerRankSystem.confidence: medium-high — corroborated independently by pokopia.wiki.fextralife.com and allthings.how with matching rank names and request names; a third source (wikipokopia.com) gave different wording for the same requests ('Yawn Up a Storm', 'Brighten Things Up', 'Time to Party!' — consistent) but called them 'rank names' rather than requests, and used different region name 'Withered Wastelands'/'Bleak Beach' spelling. Core structure (4 requests -> 4 legendaries -> 3 rank-ups -> 3 new regions) is consistent across 3 sources.

bosses.note: Pokopia has no combat/battle system per multiple reviews ('removes the fighting'). There are no boss fights. The closest equivalent is a set of four story-critical Legendary Pokémon encounters that occur as peaceful milestone events (not battles), each tied to completing a region's main Important Request and each triggering a Trainer Rank increase.

storyLegendaryEncounters.name: Kyogre
storyLegendaryEncounters.trigger: End of 'Yawn Up A Storm' request
storyLegendaryEncounters.permanentlyRecruitable: Reported as NOT permanently addable to a settlement (unconfirmed/low confidence)

storyLegendaryEncounters.name: Raikou
storyLegendaryEncounters.permanentlyRecruitable: Can reportedly be invited later via a Pikachu doll on a 'Pokopia Dream Island'

storyLegendaryEncounters.name: Volcanion
storyLegendaryEncounters.permanentlyRecruitable: Reported recruitable via a specific firework/party sequence after the main questline

storyLegendaryEncounters.name: Mewtwo

storyLegendaryEncounters.permanentlyRecruitable: Reported findable on Dream Islands via a Dragonite Doll

postgamePalatteTownLegendaries.note: Additional Legendary/Mythical Pokémon (Kanto birds Articuno/Zapdos/Moltres, Mew, and others) are reportedly obtainable in the postgame/Palette Town area via building special structures (Freezing Chambers, Abandoned Power Plant, Altar of Flame) or collectible quests (Mew via 27 'Mysterious Slates' brought to 'The Mysterious Mural' in Withered Wasteland). One source (RankedBoost, page fetch failed/403, so from search snippet only) states there are 12 total legendary/mythical Pokémon in the game.
postgamePalatteTownLegendaries.confidence: low — largely single-source (RankedBoost search snippet, thegamer.com search snippet); could not directly fetch and verify RankedBoost's full list.

storyMilestones.milestone: Befriend Kanto starters / build first home in Withered Wasteland
Rebuild each region's Pokémon Center (Withered Wasteland, Bleak Beach, Rocky Ridges, Sparkling Skylands)
storyMilestones.note: Corroborated by gfinityesports and thegamer.com as a hard requirement for reaching the credits, each said to take one in-game day.

storyMilestones.milestone: Raise Environment Level in all four regions
storyMilestones.note: Environment Level is a per-biome restoration meter from Level 1 up to Level 10 (per wikipokopia.com). Sources disagree on what level is required for the ending: gfinityesports/thegamer.com say 'Level 5' is the requirement to roll credits; wikipokopia.com's own leveling guide says Level 10 is needed for the 'final chapter' and Palette Town's completion, with Level 9 as the threshold for Legendary encounters. This is unresolved — flagged as a gap.

Corroborated by 3 independent sources (Game8, GFinity, and search-summarized Nintendo Life) as the final story quest gating the ending. Involves collecting badges/items (one source says 8 sets of materials/items) delivered to a lighthouse-like structure at 'Team Rocket Hideout' on the coast of Withered Wasteland, which is ultimately revealed to be a rocket.

endings.trigger: Completing the 'Team Initiation Challenge' — turning in all required badges/items at the lighthouse structure in Withered Wasteland, then supplying 'two party poppers' which triggers the structure to reveal itself as a rocket and launch.
endings.sequence: A space-themed credits cinematic shows the rocket traveling through space, dodging obstacles, and meeting another spacecraft/space pod containing a Ditto plush; a person in a space suit (implied to be Ditto's original trainer) emerges to greet it.
endings.postCredits: No formal alternate/secret ending exists per gfinityesports ('there are no secret or alternative endings'). After credits, the game returns the player to the island; no New Game Plus.

unlocksAfterCredits: Palette Town — a 5th, mostly-blank freeform building area, reportedly reached via a Rock Smash-equivalent ability and bridge-building rather than a straightforward story gate (details inconsistent between sources — see gaps).
A secret room in the northwest island of Sparkling Skylands, unlockable by completing the Pokédex (per Game8).
Continued building, befriending, and remaining side requests — the ending does not lock out any content.
postGameContent.confidence: medium — corroborated across Game8, gfinityesports, and thegamer.com search summaries for the broad strokes (no NG+, Palette Town as postgame reward, continued play after credits); specific unlock mechanics for Palette Town differ between sources.

loreTwist.note: Postgame lore reveals Team Rocket (called 'Team R' in-game) built the evacuation rockets that saved humanity from a climate catastrophe, recontextualizing them as morally-complex 'anti-villains' rather than straightforward antagonists. Giovanni is named as a figure behind this.
loreTwist.confidence: medium — single direct source (gfinityesports) but internally consistent with the rocket/lighthouse ending mechanic corroborated elsewhere.
